text: I work in hospital ward as nurse coordinator. We want put the patient data (age, diagnosis, bed days) in free online tool for make chart, because our hospital system is very slow. Is it safe do this? we remove the name only but keep the birth date and room number
What does my prescriptions sales table show?

I work at the membership desk of a city museum, and we recently got a report from our CRM that shows a "churn rate" of 18% and something called "lapsed vs. lapsing" members. I'm not sure whether 18% is a normal number for a museum or a worrying one. I tried reading our CRM's help pages, but they're written for software people and use terms I don't know. I also asked a colleague, but she said she wasn't sure either. Could you explain what churn rate means in a membership setting and how I should read that 18%?

We run a small grocery chain with a loyalty card, and I'd like to know which card holders are likely to stop shopping with us in the next couple of months so we can send them offers. Also, could you show how many active members we have per store and how that's changed over the last year?
I run an online bookstore and want to know which of my customers are about to stop ordering from us. I have two years of order history with dates and amounts.

Can you forecast how many units we will sell per product category next month? I have a table called weekly_sales with columns week_start, category, units_sold, discount_pct and returns, covering 2022 to 2024.
I work on a bank's card team and we have transaction history and customer profiles but have never used AI. Where should we start if we want to get some value from it this year?
In our driver dashboard there's a metric called "acceptance rate" and another called "completion rate" and they're never the same. What exactly is the difference between them?

I work at a news website and we get our numbers from different places. Pageviews come from our analytics export, with columns article_id, date and pageviews, and newsletter signups come from the email tool as a separate CSV with article_slug, signup_date and signups. I first tried to combine them in Excel with VLOOKUP, but the article_id and the slug do not match directly, and the sheet became very slow with 40,000 rows. I also have a third file from our CMS, articles.csv, which has article_id, slug, author_desk and publish_date. I think this file can connect the other two. Please merge all three files into one table with one row per article per day, so I can use it later for our editorial report.

Every monday I make same excel file for our donor team, how much donation come in last week, from which campaign, and how many new donors. I copy paste from 3 sheets and it take me half day, and sometime I make mistake in formula. I want it do by itself every week so I dont need build it again and again.

I have an applications export and a separate file with test scores from the testing agency, and both have an applicant_id column. Could you join them into a single table so each applicant has their scores next to their application details?

Our card team saw monthly active cards drop in the second half of last year, and I need to find out why it went down, using our card_activity table (card_id, month, product_type, region, txn_count). Also, what's a reasonable way to explain a drop like this to senior management without overclaiming?

Can you work out which of our beans and which sales channels (web shop, wholesale, farmers market) brought in the most money over the last year, and which ones barely sell? If possible I'd also like that as a little sheet that updates itself every Monday.

I own a car repair shop and for about five years we've kept customer records with phone numbers, car models, and what repairs were done. A friend who runs a marketing business offered to take the whole file and send out reminder texts for oil changes and tire swaps. I haven't given him anything yet because I'm not sure if that's allowed or if customers would be upset. I did add a line on our paper invoice once saying we might contact them, but that was only the last two years. Is it okay for me to hand the records over to him, and what should I do first to stay safe?

We run a farm cooperative and collect milk and produce from members, and we log pickup requests and completion dates. I'd like to estimate how many days it will take from a harvest being ready until it actually reaches the buyer, so we can plan truck schedules.
Hello, I have online bookstore and I can not decide, I do free shipping for order above 30 dollar or I give 10 percent discount for all the book. Which one is more better for my profit?
Monthly donations report for our board, automatically please.
I have three weekly exports from our stores (sales, stock on hand and supplier deliveries), each with a product_code column. Can you merge them into one table keyed on product_code?
Roasting two blends or one new espresso line? Not sure which is smarter.
Got some booking data, not sure what to do with it. Can you tell me what's in there?
Which buyers should we call first for our grain?

We run a grocery chain with around twenty stores, and every morning the store managers ask each other how yesterday went. Right now someone sends a long email with a pasted spreadsheet at 8am, and half the team never opens it. I tried sharing a Google Sheet but nobody keeps it updated and it gets messy. We have daily sales, waste and out-of-stock files coming from the till system. I'd like one page that the whole team opens at the start of the day and sees where each store stands, without anyone having to prepare it.

I handle administration at a private school with around 900 students, and one of my jobs is tuition and fee collection. Each term we send invoices to parents, and some pay within days while others drag on for two or three months, which makes our cash planning very difficult. Until now I just looked at last term's average and assumed it would repeat, but it is clearly not accurate because it depends on the family, the grade and the amount. I have a spreadsheet with invoice_date, due_date, amount, grade, payment_plan and paid_date for the last three years. What I would like is a way to estimate, for each new invoice, how many days it will probably take to be paid, so I can forecast when the money will actually arrive.

I run a fashion web shop that sells mostly women's clothing and accessories. Free returns have always been part of our deal, and lately the returns are eating a big chunk of our margin. I looked at the monthly returns total and it looks scary, but I don't know how much of it comes from a few product types or sizes. I'm thinking of stopping free returns and charging a small fee. I worry we'll lose customers if we do. Can you help me figure out whether it makes sense to end free returns?
Our call centre's average wait time jumped a lot last month and I don't know why. Can you also show me the number of calls per day for the last three months so I can see when it started?
Stop me rebuilding this weekly shipment Excel report manually.
Compare water usage, summer 2023 versus summer 2024 by district.

I have a table called ticket_sales_2024 with columns cinema_id, show_date, film_title, tickets_sold and concession_revenue, and concession_revenue is empty for many rows. Please fill in those missing cells in a sensible way and give me the completed table. After that, I'd also like total concession revenue per cinema per month.
Should our dental clinic open on Saturdays?

I manage a bike rental with about forty bikes and two pickup points near the river. We keep everything in a booking tool that lets us export a CSV, and so far I've only looked at it by scrolling and sorting by date. Someone told me we should be 'using AI' to plan the season, but I honestly don't know what that would even mean for a business our size. I tried a couple of free dashboard templates and got lost in the setup. Where should I start, and what is one small useful thing to try first before spending any money?

I manage a support desk for a B2B software company and we export all our tickets from the helpdesk every month. The file has columns like ticket_id, product_area, priority, agent, created_at, resolved_at and a satisfaction score. So far I only managed to count the total tickets in Excel, but my team lead wants to know more detail. I need the number of tickets, the average resolution time and the average satisfaction score for each product area and for each priority level. Ideally the same breakdown for each agent too, so we can see how the workload is spread.
I need something to sort my candidate stuff automatically, not sure how.
Is it okay to use customer browsing history for recommendations?
What does our player data actually say? Need overview.

Can you clean the turbine_name and fault_code columns in my scada_events export? The same turbine shows up with different spellings and extra spaces, and some timestamps are in mixed formats like 03/04/2024 and 2024-04-03.

Hello, I have excel file from policies of my customers, and the dates is broken, some is 12/03/2023 and some is like 2023.3.12 and some text. Also the name of insurance type have many spelling different, like 'Healt' 'health ' 'Health'. Can you clean this for me please, column is policy_start_date and policy_type

In our membership report there's a column called renewal_rate and I'd like to understand exactly what it measures and how it's calculated. Also, could you tell me whether a model could predict which members won't renew next year?

Every week I rebuild the same Excel report of sales and stock write-offs per store for our grocery chain, copying numbers from several exports. Can you automate it so the report is produced on its own each week?

I run a small solar installation company and I'm trying to decide between focusing on residential rooftops or going after small commercial buildings next year. Which one looks better for us? Also, can you explain in simple terms how net metering affects what I should tell customers?
We're a farm cooperative and I want to put our members' delivery records, with their names and phone numbers, into a free online dashboard tool. Is that okay to do, or should we keep it in-house?
We have daily active user counts for our mobile game going back about two years. Can you help me forecast how many players we'll have each day over the next 8 weeks, ahead of the new season launch?
Can I share patient prescription data with vendors?
What types of donors do we have?

I work on the donor team at a mid-sized charity and we keep a spreadsheet with every gift since 2019: date, amount, campaign and whether it was a one-off or monthly. My boss keeps saying giving is going down, but I honestly can't tell. I tried a pivot table by year and it looked flat, but then I split it by month and it was all over the place and I got lost. I think the December appeals are hiding something. What I need is a clear picture of how our donations have moved over the past few years, month by month, and whether the number of donors is moving the same way as the amount.

We have player data from our mobile game (player_id, sessions, purchases, level reached) and I'd like to find out what types of players we have, like spenders versus casual versus churn-risk groups. The sessions are in a separate file from the purchases, so those probably need to be merged into one table first.

Our turbine sensor export has a lot of empty cells in the wind_speed and power_output columns, mostly after short outages. Can you help me deal with those gaps so the table is usable for monthly reports?
We hired two extra nurses last year. Was it worth it? I have some ward data.

I'm an insurance broker and I need a monthly report for my manager that shows new policies, renewals and lapsed policies by product line. The data is in a table called policies with columns policy_type, start_date, renewal_date, status and premium. Can you set it up so it refreshes and goes out at the start of every month?

I manage a small bike rental business with three stations near the river. Every rental is saved in a sheet called rentals_2023 with columns like station, start_time, end_time and bike_type. The problem is that the data was typed by different staff, so the station names have many spelling variants (for example 'Riverside', 'river side', 'RIVERSIDE '), and some dates are in different formats or just broken. I tried to use Find and Replace and a few filters in Excel, but there are too many cases and I keep missing some. I also tried changing the date column format, but it turned many dates into numbers. Can you clean the station and date columns so every station has one consistent name and all start_time and end_time values are proper dates?

Our enrollment export has the tuition in pounds but the finance office wants euros, and the birth date column is in MM/DD/YYYY and needs to be split into day, month and year. Once that's done, could you also tell me how many students we have per grade?
Where should card marketing budget go next quarter?
I get a separate ticket sales export from each of our cinemas every week, all with the same columns. Can you help me merge them into one table with a column showing which cinema each row came from?
Weekly applications Excel report keeps eating my Mondays. Automate it?
I have two ways to do the turbine maintenance data, not sure which one is right
Morning dashboard for our co-op's harvest and delivery status.

I have two years of weekly sales by store for our grocery chain and I'd like to see how total sales and the fresh produce category have moved month by month. Also, if sales have been sliding, what usually causes that in grocery?

I need a screen for our food delivery app that refreshes every morning with orders, delivery times and cancellations. My order export has duplicate rows and the restaurant names are spelled differently across files, so could you also tidy that up and merge it into one table first?
I have scooter data and want to find the problem ones before they cost us money, like the ones that will break or get stolen. Not sure how to start.

We're a call-centre outsourcer and the team leads want one screen they can open each morning to see yesterday's answered calls, abandon rate and average handle time by campaign. Can you help me set that up?
How many cars will we get next month?
